summary: Can a string be segmented into a sequence of dictionary words?
mainInsight: dp[i] is true if the prefix s[:i] can be segmented: dp[0] = True and dp[i] = any(dp[j] and s[j:i] in words for j < i). Limit j to the maximum word length and keep words in a set. Memoised DFS is the top-down version.

promptVariants: Why is memoisation (or DP) required, and how can the inner loop be bounded?
What makes the plain recursion exponential?
cards.answer: The same suffix is explored through many different segmentations (e.g. 'aaaa...' with words 'a', 'aa'), so without caching the recursion is exponential. Bounding j to at most the maximum word length avoids useless long substring checks and gives O(n * L) set lookups.
